text: A cross-lingual part-of-speech tagger that leverages the power of disparate sources of distant supervision has been developed. This model is capable of scaling to hundreds of low-resource languages, making it a practical solution for many language-related challenges. The tagger employs a uniform framework that integrates annotation projection, instance selection, tag dictionaries, morphological lexicons, and distributed representations. The result is a simple yet highly effective approach that achieves a new state of the art, even without access to any gold annotated data.

label: acl
text: The Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model is essentially a joint language model conditioned on both the source sentence and partial translation. Therefore, the NMT model naturally involves the mechanism of the Language Model (LM) that predicts the next token only based on partial translation. Despite its success, NMT still suffers from the hallucination problem, generating fluent but inadequate translations. The main reason is that NMT pays excessive attention to the partial translation while neglecting the source sentence to some extent, namely overconfidence of the LM. Accordingly, we define the Margin between the NMT and the LM, calculated by subtracting the predicted probability of the LM from that of the NMT model for each token. The Margin is negatively correlated to the overconfidence degree of the LM. Based on the property, we propose a Margin-based Token-level Objective (MTO) and a Margin-based Sentence-level Objective (MSO) to maximize the Margin for preventing the LM from being overconfident. Experiments on WMT14 English-to-German, WMT19 Chinese-to-English, and WMT14 English-to-French translation tasks demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach, with 1.36, 1.50, and 0.63 BLEU improvements, respectively, compared to the Transformer baseline. The human evaluation further verifies that our approaches improve translation adequacy as well as fluency.

label: acl
text: The Neural Machine Translation (NMT) model is a joint language model that is conditioned on both the source sentence and partial translation. As a result, the NMT model incorporates the mechanism of the Language Model (LM) that predicts the next token based on the partial translation only. Despite its success, the NMT still faces the challenge of generating fluent but inadequate translations, known as the hallucination problem. This is due to the NMT's overconfidence in the LM, which causes it to pay excessive attention to the partial translation while neglecting the source sentence. To address this issue, we introduce the Margin between the NMT and LM, calculated by subtracting the predicted probability of the LM from that of the NMT model for each token. This Margin is negatively correlated with the overconfidence of the LM. To prevent the LM from being overconfident, we propose two objectives: the Margin-based Token-level Objective (MTO) and the Margin-based Sentence-level Objective (MSO). Our approach has been tested on three translation tasks (WMT14 English-to-German, WMT19 Chinese-to-English, and WMT14 English-to-French) and has shown significant improvements, with BLEU scores of 1.36, 1.50, and 0.63, respectively, compared to the Transformer baseline. Furthermore, human evaluations have confirmed that our approach improves both translation adequacy and fluency.

label: coling
text: In this work, we aim at developing an unsupervised abstractive summarization system in the multi-document setting. We design a paraphrastic sentence fusion model which jointly performs sentence fusion and paraphrasing using skip-gram word embedding model at the sentence level. Our model improves the information coverage and at the same time abstractiveness of the generated sentences. We conduct our experiments on the human-generated multi-sentence compression datasets and evaluate our system on several newly proposed Machine Translation (MT) evaluation metrics. Furthermore, we apply our sentence level model to implement an abstractive multi-document summarization system where documents usually contain a related set of sentences. We also propose an optimal solution for the classical summary length limit problem which was not addressed in the past research. For the document level summary, we conduct experiments on the datasets of two different domains (e.g., news article and user reviews) which are well suited for multi-document abstractive summarization. Our experiments demonstrate that the methods bring significant improvements over the state-of-the-art methods.

text: Our work focuses on developing an unsupervised abstractive summarization system for multi-document settings. We introduce a paraphrastic sentence fusion model that combines sentence fusion and paraphrasing using a skip-gram word embedding model at the sentence level. This model enhances the information coverage and abstractiveness of the generated sentences. We evaluate our system on human-generated multi-sentence compression datasets and various newly proposed Machine Translation evaluation metrics. Additionally, we apply our sentence-level model to create an abstractive multi-document summarization system for documents containing related sentences. We also provide an optimal solution for the classical summary length limit problem, which has not been addressed in previous research. Our experiments on two different domains (news articles and user reviews) demonstrate significant improvements over state-of-the-art methods.

label: acl
text: Machine reading comprehension (MRC) is a crucial task in natural language processing and has achieved remarkable advancements. However, most of the neural MRC models are still far from robust and fail to generalize well in real-world applications. In order to comprehensively verify the robustness and generalization of MRC models, we introduce a real-world Chinese dataset – DuReader_robust . It is designed to evaluate the MRC models from three aspects: over-sensitivity, over-stability and generalization. Comparing to previous work, the instances in DuReader_robust are natural texts, rather than the altered unnatural texts. It presents the challenges when applying MRC models to real-world applications. The experimental results show that MRC models do not perform well on the challenge test set. Moreover, we analyze the behavior of existing models on the challenge test set, which may provide suggestions for future model development. The dataset and codes are publicly available at https://github.com/baidu/DuReader.

label: acl
text: Machine reading comprehension (MRC) is a critical task in natural language processing that has made significant advancements. Despite this, most neural MRC models are still not robust and struggle to generalize well in real-world applications. To thoroughly evaluate the robustness and generalization of MRC models, we introduce the DuReader_robust dataset, a real-world Chinese dataset designed to assess the models from three perspectives: over-sensitivity, over-stability, and generalization. Unlike previous work, the instances in DuReader_robust are natural texts, not altered unnatural texts, presenting real-world challenges for MRC models. The results of our experiments show that MRC models perform poorly on the challenge test set, and our analysis of existing models' behavior on this set provides insights for future model development. The dataset and code are available for public use at https://github.com/baidu/DuReader.

label: acl
text: Distant supervision for relation extraction provides uniform bag labels for each sentence inside the bag, while accurate sentence labels are important for downstream applications that need the exact relation type. Directly using bag labels for sentence-level training will introduce much noise, thus severely degrading performance. In this work, we propose the use of negative training (NT), in which a model is trained using complementary labels regarding that “the instance does not belong to these complementary labels”. Since the probability of selecting a true label as a complementary label is low, NT provides less noisy information. Furthermore, the model trained with NT is able to separate the noisy data from the training data. Based on NT, we propose a sentence-level framework, SENT, for distant relation extraction. SENT not only filters the noisy data to construct a cleaner dataset, but also performs a re-labeling process to transform the noisy data into useful training data, thus further benefiting the model's performance. Experimental results show the significant improvement of the proposed method over previous methods on sentence-level evaluation and de-noise effect.

label: acl
text: The use of distant supervision for relation extraction provides uniform bag labels for each sentence within the bag. However, accurate sentence-level labels are crucial for downstream applications that require specific relation types. Directly using bag labels for sentence-level training can result in a significant amount of noise and negatively impact performance. To address this issue, we propose the use of negative training (NT), in which the model is trained using complementary labels indicating that the instance does not belong to these complementary labels. This approach provides less noisy information as the probability of selecting the true label as a complementary label is low. The model trained with NT is able to effectively separate noisy data from the training data. Our proposed sentence-level framework, SENT, leverages NT to filter noisy data and construct a cleaner dataset. Additionally, SENT performs a re-labeling process to transform noisy data into useful training data, further improving the model's performance. Our experimental results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed method compared to previous methods in terms of sentence-level evaluation and de-noising effect.

label: acl
text: Document date is essential for many important tasks, such as document retrieval, summarization, event detection, etc. While existing approaches for these tasks assume accurate knowledge of the document date, this is not always available, especially for arbitrary documents from the Web. Document Dating is a challenging problem which requires inference over the temporal structure of the document. Prior document dating systems have largely relied on handcrafted features while ignoring such document-internal structures. In this paper, we propose NeuralDater, a Graph Convolutional Network (GCN) based document dating approach which jointly exploits syntactic and temporal graph structures of document in a principled way. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first application of deep learning for the problem of document dating. Through extensive experiments on real-world datasets, we find that NeuralDater significantly outperforms state-of-the-art baseline by 19% absolute (45% relative) accuracy points.

label: acl
text: The date of a document is crucial for a range of important tasks, such as document retrieval, summarization, and event detection. However, existing methods for these tasks often assume accurate knowledge of the document date, which is not always available, especially for arbitrary documents from the web. Document dating is a difficult problem that requires inferring the temporal structure of a document. Previous document dating systems have mostly relied on handcrafted features and ignored the internal structures of the document. This paper presents NeuralDater, a graph convolutional network (GCN) based approach to document dating that jointly exploits the syntactic and temporal graph structures of the document. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first use of deep learning for document dating. Through extensive experiments on real-world datasets, we show that NeuralDater outperforms state-of-the-art baselines by 19% absolute (45% relative) accuracy points.

label: coling
text: Although the fluency of automatically generated abstractive summaries has improved significantly with advanced methods, the inconsistency that remains in summarization is recognized as an issue to be addressed. In this study, we propose a methodology for localizing inconsistency errors in summarization. A synthetic dataset that contains a variety of factual errors likely to be produced by a common summarizer is created by applying sentence fusion, compression, and paraphrasing operations. In creating the dataset, we automatically label erroneous phrases and the dependency relations between them as “inconsistent,” which can contribute to detecting errors more adequately than existing models that rely only on dependency arc-level labels. Subsequently, this synthetic dataset is employed as weak supervision to train a model called SumPhrase, which jointly localizes errors in a summary and their corresponding sentences in the source document. The empirical results demonstrate that our SumPhrase model can detect factual errors in summarization more effectively than existing weakly supervised methods owing to the phrase-level labeling. Moreover, the joint identification of error-corresponding original sentences is proven to be effective in improving error detection accuracy.

label: coling
text: The fluency of automatically generated abstractive summaries has improved significantly with advanced methods, but the inconsistency that still remains in summarization is a problem that needs to be addressed. In this study, we propose a methodology for identifying inconsistent errors in summarization. We created a synthetic dataset that contains a variety of factual errors likely to be produced by a common summarizer, using sentence fusion, compression, and paraphrasing operations. To create the dataset, we automatically labeled erroneous phrases and their dependency relations as "inconsistent," which contributes to more accurate error detection than existing models that rely only on dependency arc-level labels. Our synthetic dataset was used as weak supervision to train the SumPhrase model, which can jointly localize errors in a summary and their corresponding sentences in the source document. The empirical results show that our SumPhrase model is more effective in detecting factual errors in summarization than existing weakly supervised methods, thanks to the phrase-level labeling. Additionally, the joint identification of the original sentences corresponding to errors has been proven to improve error detection accuracy.

label: acl
text: Text-to-image retrieval is an essential task in cross-modal information retrieval, i.e., retrieving relevant images from a large and unlabelled dataset given textual queries. In this paper, we propose VisualSparta, a novel (Visual-text Sparse Transformer Matching) model that shows significant improvement in terms of both accuracy and efficiency. VisualSparta is capable of outperforming previous state-of-the-art scalable methods in MSCOCO and Flickr30K. We also show that it achieves substantial retrieving speed advantages, i.e., for a 1 million image index, VisualSparta using CPU gets ~391X speedup compared to CPU vector search and ~5.4X speedup compared to vector search with GPU acceleration. Experiments show that this speed advantage even gets bigger for larger datasets because VisualSparta can be efficiently implemented as an inverted index. To the best of our knowledge, VisualSparta is the first transformer-based text-to-image retrieval model that can achieve real-time searching for large-scale datasets, with significant accuracy improvement compared to previous state-of-the-art methods.

label: acl
text: Text-to-image retrieval is a crucial aspect of cross-modal information retrieval, which involves finding relevant images from a vast and unlabeled dataset based on textual queries. In this paper, we present VisualSparta, a novel Visual-text Sparse Transformer Matching model that demonstrates substantial improvements in accuracy and efficiency. Our model outperforms previous state-of-the-art scalable methods in MSCOCO and Flickr30K. Additionally, VisualSparta offers substantial retrieval speed advantages, with a 1 million image index resulting in a ~391X speedup compared to CPU vector search and ~5.4X speedup compared to GPU-accelerated vector search. Our experiments reveal that this speed advantage increases even further for larger datasets as VisualSparta can be implemented as an inverted index, making it highly efficient. To the best of our knowledge, VisualSparta is the first transformer-based text-to-image retrieval model that can achieve real-time searching for large-scale datasets with improved accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods.

text: Research on the application of NLP in symbol-based Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) tools for improving social interaction support is scarce. We contribute a novel method for generating context-related vocabulary from photographs of personally relevant events aimed at supporting people with language impairments in retelling their past experiences. Performance was calculated with information retrieval concepts on the relevance of vocabulary generated for communicating a corpus of 9730 narrative phrases about events depicted in 1946 photographs. In comparison to a baseline generation composed of frequent English words, our method generated vocabulary with a 4.6 gain in mean average precision, regardless of the level of contextual information in the input photographs, and 6.9 for photographs in which contextual information was extracted correctly. We conclude by discussing how our findings provide insights for system optimization and usage.

label: acl
text: The research on the use of NLP in symbol-based Augmentative and Alternative Communication (AAC) tools for enhancing social interaction support is limited. We present a new approach for creating context-specific vocabulary from photographs of personal events, aimed at assisting individuals with language impairments in relaying their past experiences. The performance was evaluated using information retrieval methods, based on the relevance of vocabulary generated for 9730 narrative phrases about events depicted in 1946 photographs. Our method generated vocabulary with a 4.6 increase in mean average precision compared to a baseline of frequent English words, regardless of the level of contextual information in the input photographs. The results were even better, with a 6.9 increase, for photographs with correctly extracted contextual information. Finally, we discuss how our findings provide valuable insights for optimizing system usage and performance.

label: emnlp
text: Neural machine translation (NMT) models are usually trained with the word-level loss using the teacher forcing algorithm, which not only evaluates the translation improperly but also suffers from exposure bias. Sequence-level training under the reinforcement framework can mitigate the problems of the word-level loss, but its performance is unstable due to the high variance of the gradient estimation. On these grounds, we present a method with a differentiable sequence-level training objective based on probabilistic n-gram matching which can avoid the reinforcement framework. In addition, this method performs greedy search in the training which uses the predicted words as context just as at inference to alleviate the problem of exposure bias. Experiment results on the NIST Chinese-to-English translation tasks show that our method significantly outperforms the reinforcement-based algorithms and achieves an improvement of 1.5 BLEU points on average over a strong baseline system.

label: emnlp
text: Neural machine translation (NMT) models are typically trained with a word-level loss using the teacher forcing algorithm. However, this method can lead to incorrect evaluations and exposure bias. To address these issues, sequence-level training with a reinforcement framework has been proposed. However, this approach can be unstable due to the high variance in gradient estimation. To avoid these problems, we present a differentiable sequence-level training objective based on probabilistic n-gram matching. Our method also uses greedy search during training, incorporating predicted words as context, which helps to alleviate the exposure bias issue. Our experiments on the NIST Chinese-to-English translation tasks show that our method outperforms reinforcement-based algorithms, achieving an average improvement of 1.5 BLEU points over a strong baseline system.
